## Part 1 — Python library

### Library 1 — your first price path

```python
from mktsim import basic_id_sim_1

path = basic_id_sim_1(375, 100.0, seed=1)
```

```text
ticks=375 start=100.00 end=96.40 min=95.95 max=101.65 return=-3.60%
```

### Library 2 — profitability biases the flow, not the fate

```python
from mktsim import basic_id_sim_1

for profit in (1.0, 0.0, -1.0):
    ups = sum(1 for s in range(60)
              if basic_id_sim_1(200, 100.0, profit, seed=s)[-1] >= 100.0)
    print(profit, f"{ups}/60 up")
```

```text
1.0 47/60 up
0.0 31/60 up
-1.0 12/60 up
```

`+1` finishes up most of the time, `-1` mostly down, `0.0` is a
coin flip — but single paths can always go against the bias.

### Library 3 — prices plus per-tick volumes

```python
from mktsim import basic_id_sim_1

prices, volumes = basic_id_sim_1(10, 100.0, seed=7, return_volumes=True)
for t, (p, v) in enumerate(zip(prices, volumes)):
    print(f"tick={t} price={p:.2f} volume={v}")
```

### Library 4 — ticks into OHLCV bars

```python
from mktsim import basic_id_sim_1, ticks_to_ohlcv

prices, volumes = basic_id_sim_1(20, 100.0, seed=7, return_volumes=True)
for b in ticks_to_ohlcv(prices, volumes, bars=4):
    print(b)
```

```text
{'bar': 1, 'open': 100.0, 'high': 100.0, 'low': 99.75, 'close': 99.8, 'volume': 149}
{'bar': 2, 'open': 99.8, 'high': 99.8, 'low': 99.7, 'close': 99.7, 'volume': 136}

{'bar': 4, 'open': 99.8, 'high': 100.35, 'low': 99.8, 'close': 100.35, 'volume': 245}
```

### Library 5 — CSV export from Python

```python
from mktsim import basic_id_sim_1, bars_to_csv, simulate_ohlcv, ticks_to_csv

prices, volumes = basic_id_sim_1(20, 100.0, seed=7, return_volumes=True)
ticks_to_csv(prices, volumes, "ticks.csv")
bars_to_csv(simulate_ohlcv(basic_id_sim_1, 20, 100.0, 0.0, seed=7, bars=4), "bars.csv")
```

`ticks.csv` (head):



### Library 6 — growth bands cap every step

```python
from mktsim import basic_id_sim_2

path = basic_id_sim_2(120, 50.0, 0.5, max_growth=0.01, min_growth=-0.01, seed=3)
steps = [path[i] / path[i - 1] - 1 for i in range(1, len(path))]
print(f"worst step: {min(steps):+.4%} / {max(steps):+.4%}")
```

```text
worst step: -0.3865% / +0.5825%
```

No single tick moved more than ±1% (start=50.00, end=52.85).

### Library 7 — a full session with an overnight gap

```python
from mktsim import basic_id_sim_3

path = basic_id_sim_3(375, 100.0, seed=5)  # 100.0 is the *previous close*
print(f"prev_close=100.00 open={path[0]:.2f} close={path[-1]:.2f}")
print(f"overnight gap={100 * (path[0] / 100 - 1):+.2f}% day range={min(path):.2f}-{max(path):.2f}")
```

```text
prev_close=100.00 open=99.90 close=90.00
overnight gap=-0.10% day range=89.95-101.45
```

### Library 8 — day regimes change the character

```python
from mktsim import basic_id_sim_3

for regime in ("normal", "trend", "range", "event", "calm"):
    path = basic_id_sim_3(200, 100.0, regime=regime, seed=7)
    print(f"{regime:6} end={path[-1]:7.2f} range={min(path):6.2f}-{max(path):6.2f}")
```

```text
normal end= 100.75 range= 95.00-102.25
trend  end= 100.85 range= 90.15-104.05
range  end=  98.55 range= 97.05-100.35
event  end=  90.00 range= 89.95-101.05
calm   end=  99.35 range= 98.80-100.15
```

Same seed, five personalities — including `event` slamming the 10%
lower circuit band (90.00) while `calm` barely leaves the open.

### Library 9 — targeting +5% on average

```python
from mktsim import basic_id_sim_4
import statistics

ends = [basic_id_sim_4(200, 100.0, 0.0, 0.05, seed=s)[-1] for s in range(40)]
print(f"mean={statistics.mean(ends):.2f} (target 105.00) "
      f"worst={min(ends):.2f} best={max(ends):.2f}")
```

```text
mean=105.63 (target 105.00) worst=101.05 best=111.80
```

### Library 10 — seeds make everything reproducible

```python
from mktsim import basic_id_sim_1

a = basic_id_sim_1(50, 100.0, seed=42)
b = basic_id_sim_1(50, 100.0, seed=42)
c = basic_id_sim_1(50, 100.0, seed=43)
print(a == b, a == c)  # True False
```

```text
True False
```

### Library 11 — a full session bar record

```python
from mktsim import adv_id_sim_1, bars_ex_to_csv

bars = adv_id_sim_1(12, 100.0, 1.0, seed=7)
print(len(bars), "bars x", len(bars[0]), "fields")
print(bars[3])
bars_ex_to_csv(bars, "session.csv")
```

### Library 12 — steering the mean with target_pct

```python
from mktsim import adv_id_sim_1
import statistics

for target in (5.0, 0.0, -5.0):
    ends = [adv_id_sim_1(150, 100.0, target, seed=s)[-1]["close"]
            for s in range(15)]
    print(f"target={target:+.1f}% mean={statistics.mean(ends):.2f}")
```

```text
target=+5.0% mean=104.12
target=+0.0% mean=100.06
target=-5.0% mean=96.01
```



```powershell

```

```text
[2/3] basic_interaday.basic_id_sim_4 n=60 start=100.00 end=103.35 -> sim_002.csv
[3/3] basic_interaday.basic_id_sim_4 n=60 start=100.00 end=108.05 -> sim_003.csv
runs=3 mean_end=104.98 ± 2.66 up=100.0% avg_return=+4.98% best=108.05 worst=103.35
```

Seeds `1, 2, 3` produced `sim_001.csv`, `sim_002.csv`, `sim_003.csv`.

### CLI 6 — the REPL, same flow interactively

Start with `mktsim`, then:
```text
share-market simulator -- type 'help' for commands.
sim> use basic_id_sim_1
using basic_interaday.basic_id_sim_1 (7 params) -- 'show' to inspect, 'set' to change.
sim> set nums 20
nums = 20
sim> set initial_price 100
initial_price = 100
sim> set seed 7
seed = 7
sim> run
[basic_interaday.basic_id_sim_1] n=20 start=100.00 end=100.35 min=99.65 max=100.35 return=+0.35% bars=20
sim> show
  nums = 20  [default (required)]
  initial_price = 100  [default (required)]
  profitability = 0.0  [default 0.0]
  seed = 7  [default None]
  tick_size = 0.05  [default 0.05]
  base_tick_vol = 0.0012  [default 0.0012]
  return_volumes = False  [default False]
  [bars = 75]
sim> quit
```
